claims.claim: It's original 650 Watts 144 cell direct Canadian used solar panel
claims.evidence: The witness photo shows multiple rectangular solar panels on a frame, but the panel model/ratings and any readable markings (e.g., 144-cell layout, wattage label) are not readable.

claims.claim: Battery is new, holds charge for 8 hours
claims.evidence: The witness report/photo set shows solar panels on a frame; no battery is shown or described in the observations.
No repair history or internal/hidden damage indicators are visible in the provided photo; only general surface condition is mentioned.

risks.risk: Total system wattage may be less than claimed (panel count/wiring/ratings not readable). This directly affects value.
risks.proof: A clear close-up of each panel’s label/specs (watt rating and cell count) plus a shot showing the full array layout (how many panels and how they are wired/connected).
risks.if_unproven: Price as a used solar panel array with unknown total wattage (worst-case: lower wattage and/or mixed/uncertain ratings).

risks.risk: Performance degradation (micro-cracks, delamination, hot spots) may not be visible from the single angle; surface can look fine while output is weak.
risks.proof: A working output test: measure voltage/current under sunlight or provide an IV curve / multimeter readings at the panel terminals (or a controller/inverter output reading) showing real power.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not performance-tested (worst-case: reduced output).

risks.risk: Electrical compatibility and safety (connectors/cables, grounding, frame corrosion) may be poor and add cost to make it usable.
risks.proof: Close-ups of junction box, MC4 connectors/cables, and frame/mounting hardware including grounding points; check for rust/corrosion and cable condition.
risks.if_unproven: Price as needing possible replacement of connectors/cables or basic electrical work.

risks.risk: Battery claim cannot be validated; if the battery is not actually new or capacity is low, the system value drops sharply.
risks.proof: Photos of the battery label/model/age, plus a capacity/health test (e.g., BMS screen readings, voltage under load, or a capacity test report).
risks.if_unproven: Price as an unknown/possibly used battery (worst-case: reduced capacity or not holding charge).

risks.risk: Missing system components (charge controller/inverter/batteries/cables) may mean the buyer is not getting a complete working setup.
risks.proof: A full inventory photo showing everything included: charge controller, inverter (if any), battery type/quantity, cables, fuses/breakers, mounting rails, and any manuals/receipts.
risks.if_unproven: Price as panels-only (or as incomplete kit) until inclusion is confirmed.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the panel nameplate/spec label(s) showing wattage and cell count (144-cell) for each panel (or at least one clearly representative panel if identical).
Photo showing the full array: exact number of panels and how they are connected (series/parallel) and the total configuration.
Close-ups of junction box, MC4 connectors, and all visible cables; include grounding/mounting hardware shots.
A performance test: IV curve or real output measurement under load/sunlight (controller/inverter reading is acceptable).
Photos of the battery (label/model/age) and a capacity/health indicator or voltage-under-load test to confirm it holds charge for the stated duration.
Confirm what else is included (charge controller, inverter, cables, fuses/breakers) with a full set photo.
response.reason: The witness confirms solar panels on a frame, but the key details needed to price the claimed wattage/cell count and to validate the battery claim are not readable or not shown. Without those proofs, a worst-case price would be too uncertain to set confidently.
